CANONICAL_NAME.value: Redlock (antirez, 2014) as redlock-py, with Debian's redis-server as the lock store -- a lease-based distributed mutex, and the design Kleppmann's 2016 analysis argued is unsafe for correctness-critical use

VERSION.value: github.com/SPSCommerce/redlock-py master as of 2026-09-13 (commit in hashes); redis-server 7.0 (Debian bookworm) at run time

value.lineage: A LEASE-based distributed mutex: acquire a key with a TTL on a majority of N independent Redis instances within a validity window; release by a check-and-delete script. Proposed by Antirez (redis.io/topics/distlock, 2014); criticised by Martin Kleppmann ('How to do distributed locking', 2016) for depending on bounded clock drift and process pauses, with Antirez's reply ('Is Redlock safe?'). Preserved as a runnable lease mechanism AND as a documented contested design (Phase 9: incorrect timing assumption).

value.built_to: grant one client at a time exclusive access to a resource across machines, with a lease so a crashed holder cannot block forever
value.pressure: crashes of holders, network delay, clock drift, process pauses (GC) -- the last two are exactly the contested assumptions
value.success_means: mutual exclusion while the lease is valid; liveness after a holder dies

value.pressure: partial failure, unbounded delay, unsynchronised clocks
value.failure_condition: two holders at once after a pause or clock jump (Kleppmann's scenario); or permanent blocking without a lease
